newsitem.title: FRANCE: France signs accord on Future Large Aircraft.
newsitem.headline: France signs accord on Future Large Aircraft.

text.p: France's air force chief of staff has approved operating specifications planned for Europe's planned Future Large Aircraft (FLA), the air force said on Wednesday.

It said in a statement that General Rannou had signed the European Staff Requirement (ESR) agreement, which sums up the technical details for the transport aircraft and is due to be signed by all eight countries taking part in the project.
Building the FLA, it said, must draw on innovative methods inspired by civil aviation practices.

French Defence Minister Charles Millon, the statement said, had won the approval of most partners to seek a firm commitment from the countries concerned that would yield cost savings on the plane and guarantee the timetable would be respected.
The first FLA is due in the year 2002 and the first French planes are due to be ready in 2004-2005.

French President Jacques Chirac pledged on Friday that France would stick to its commitments on militay procurement including the FLA, and added that he was convinced Europeans nations would build it.

State-owned aerospace group SNI Aerospatiale has suggested building the FLA jointly with seven other European partners but since France dropped development funding, the company has been looking at commercial funding for the project.
